questions.question: Which coronary artery provides the posterior descending artery (PDA) in a 'right-dominant' circulation?
questions.detail: Circulation is defined by which artery gives rise to the PDA and the posterolateral branches; this is the RCA in approximately 85% of people.

questions.question: An Agatston score (calcium score) of 101–400 is categorized as:
Which coronary anomaly is classified as 'malignant' due to its high risk of sudden cardiac death during exercise?
choices: RCA arising from the left sinus with a retroaortic course
LAD arising from the right sinus with an interarterial course
Circumflex arising from the right sinus with a retroaortic course
questions.detail: An interarterial course (between the aorta and pulmonary artery) is 'malignant' because the vessel can be compressed during physical exertion.

questions.question: 'ALCAPA' (Bland-White-Garland syndrome) describes which anomalous connection?
choices: Right coronary arising from the pulmonary artery
Left coronary arising from the pulmonary artery
Circumflex arising from the right sinus
Coronary artery to right atrium fistula
questions.detail: ALCAPA involves the left coronary artery originating from the pulmonary artery, leading to 'steal' and potential MI in infancy.

questions.question: According to the CAD-RADS classification, a CAD-RADS 3 score represents:
Which CT plaque feature is highly associated with 'vulnerable plaque' and a higher risk of acute coronary syndrome?
questions.detail: High-risk features include positive remodeling, low-attenuation (lipid) core, and the napkin-ring sign (low density core with high density rim).

questions.question: Myocardial bridging most commonly involves which segment of which coronary artery?
questions.detail: Myocardial bridging occurs when a segment of a coronary artery (usually the mid-LAD) takes an intramyocardial course.

questions.question: A coronary artery fistula is an abnormal connection between a coronary artery and:
questions.detail: Coronary fistulas are connections to any low-pressure structure (chambers, PA, SVC) and are seen in 0.1–0.2% of patients.

questions.question: What is the most common benign coronary anomaly?
choices: Retroaortic circumflex from the right sinus
questions.detail: This is a common benign variant where the LCx arises from the right side and courses behind the aorta.

questions.question: What is the '17-segment' model used for in cardiac imaging?
choices: Standardized nomenclature for the left ventricular myocardium
questions.detail: The 17-segment model provides a uniform way to report regional wall motion or perfusion abnormalities.

questions.question: 'Dual-source' CT is particularly useful in cardiac imaging because it provides:
choices: Better temporal resolution for high heart rates
Improved spatial resolution for distal vessels
questions.detail: Dual-source CT uses two tubes at 90 degrees to acquire data faster, significantly improving temporal resolution.

questions.question: In coronary CTA, 'prospective' ECG-gating differs from 'retrospective' gating by:
choices: Pulsing the X-ray beam only during a portion of the cardiac cycle (lowering dose)
Acquiring data throughout the entire cycle
Producing a full cine loop of wall motion
questions.detail: Prospective gating (step-and-shoot) significantly reduces radiation but does not allow for functional/cine evaluation.
